task1.title: Female members of parliament in five European countries, 2000-2012
task1.prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of female members of parliament in five European countries from 2000 to 2012.

chartDesc.title: Female members of parliament in five European countries, 2000–2012
chartDesc.overview: Overall, the proportion of female MPs increased in all five European countries over the 12-year period. Belgium ended with the highest percentage of female parliamentarians, while Italy experienced the most dramatic increase between 2004 and 2008.
keyFeatures: Belgium showed a substantial increase from about 23% in 2000 to nearly 38% in 2012, becoming the highest of all five countries.
Italy had the lowest starting point at approximately 2% in 2000–2004, but saw a sharp rise to 23% by 2008, matching the UK by 2012.
Germany maintained a steady line starting at 31% in 2000 and slightly increasing to 33% in 2012.
Spain rose rapidly from 28% in 2000 to peak at 36% in 2004, stabilizing at around 35% through 2012.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
